newsitem.title: USA: U.S. judge allows new trial in 1971 baby death.
newsitem.headline: U.S. judge allows new trial in 1971 baby death.

text.p: A judge cleared the way Friday for a new trial of a man accused of killing his stepson in 1971 and blaming the death on the infant's sister, who was two years old at the time.

Dekalb Superior Court Judge Hilton Fuller said he would allow a new trial for Jan Barry Sandlin, who was charged with murder in December after a decade-long effort by Tracy Rhame to clear her name in the case.
The judge declared a mistrial Monday after Rhame admitted defying the judge's order not to watch the case on television.
In a brief written decision, Fuller said he would permit another trial, but he added: "If trial events convince the judge that the trial is fundamentally unfair, another mistrial will result."

The 1971 death of four-month-old Matthew Stephen Golder was declared an accident at the time. Tracy Rhame said she had been unfairly blamed for pushing her four-month-old half-brother out of his crib.
Prosecutors said they were prepared to retry Sandlin, who is serving a life prison term in Florida for armed robbery.

Rhame admitted she watched her mother's testimony on Court TV last week, despite Fuller's order not to do so. Sandlin's attorney argued that Rhame's memory of dates and events had become tainted by watching the televised trial.
Fuller said that, despite the mistrial, the court clearly established that Rhame was not responsible for her brother's death.
